script: High‑profile visit ruined: I exposed the supermarket's secret heatwave disaster.. It was a scorching Saturday and I was stocking the non‑food aisle at the supermarket. The air‑con was turned off—classic summer routine. The next day, the big execs were coming for a walk‑around, so we were hustling to make everything look spotless. I was helping a customer find something in the warehouse. On my way back, I spotted a life‑size cricket toy on the floor. I thought, "Nice, I'll grab that later." I tucked it in my mind and kept moving. When I bent to pick it up, the toy shifted. I froze. It wasn't a toy—it was a real cricket. I heard a voice behind me: a sweet old lady from the next aisle, barely on shift, rushing toward me with her hair in her hands. I turned, and there were five more crickets crawling down the aisle, one even landing in her hair. We'd never turned the air‑con on in that section, but they were testing it for the exec visit. The vents had been a cricket nest for weeks, and now the unit blew a rain of bugs onto the floor. I stared at the chaos, thinking, "This is not the kind of 'I am not paid enough' moment I expected." Customers started circling, asking what was happening. I just pointed and said, "We've got work crickets." The shoppers stared, baffled. Our section leader walked over, thinking there was a customer complaint. We explained the bug invasion, and she joined our "I hate bugs" club. Security showed up, looking confused and helpless. There we were: me, the bakery lady, the section leader, two security guards, and a handful of bewildered customers. Then a bakery worker sauntered over with a huge box, scooped every cricket like a pro, and walked past us, nodding like a champ. She said, "My lizard will feed well tonight," and disappeared. That's the day the supermarket tried to recreate the Plague of Egypt—with crickets instead of locusts—on a lazy Sunday. I left the job, but whenever I shop at that store, I still glance at the air‑con, just in case it decides to unleash another insect apocalypse.
